description: The database client every command line junkie deserves.

summary.one_liner: dblab is a terminal UI database client written in Go for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite3, Oracle and SQL Server, distributed as a single binary.
summary.what_it_does: Provides an interactive TUI with a sidebar tree of databases, schemas and tables, and a result set panel showing table data, columns, indexes and constraints. The query editor is Vim-style with normal and insert modes, motions, undo/redo, visual mode and search. Multiple semicolon-separated statements run concurrently in separate result tabs, and ctrl+r runs only the statement on the cursor line. It supports connection profiles saved with --save-as (passwords stored in the OS keyring), a persisted query history, a read-only mode via --readonly, and SSH tunnels for connections. Configuration is via flags, a .dblab.yaml file, or connection URLs, with eight color themes and per-panel key bindings.
use_cases: browse and query a PostgreSQL database from the terminal
explore a local SQLite file without installing a GUI
safely browse a production database in read-only mode
connect to a remote database through an SSH tunnel
save and reuse database connection profiles
run several SQL statements at once and compare results in tabs
how_to_run: dblab --host localhost --user myuser --db users --pass password --ssl disable --port 5432 --driver postgres --limit 50
notable: Vim-style query editor built on the goeditor modal-editing engine
Runs multiple SQL statements concurrently, each result in its own tab
Connection profiles with passwords stored in the OS keyring
Read-only mode forces the database session read-only across five drivers
Active schema picker (ctrl+s) for PostgreSQL and Oracle
caveats: Schema switching and the schema picker are limited to PostgreSQL and Oracle
Multi-statement batches are capped at 5 statements
There is no pagination in the result set; large tables require manual OFFSET/LIMIT queries
